questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial to me that by going on exchange at the University of Edinburgh I could perceive fields within Anthropology that were not possible at the University of Copenhagen to the same extend.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. The University of Edinburgh and the University of Copenhagen both sent several emails with information as well as when action was needed to do apply for courses etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were a couple of introduction meetings. And email to the student advisor was available at all times.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite a challenge actually since the housing in Edinburgh can be quite expensive and difficult. We got lucky and found something online which ended up being perfect. However, I would not necessarily recommend doing it like that. Can be quite sketchy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be hard to find something. The distance from campus can be a little long and requires using public transport like the busses. Housing is expensive in general.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course registration process was very different than what I have been used to in Denmark. The whole thing is online, but at first when you apply for classes before arriving you do not know how they are scheduled, which caused me and my fellow exchange students to have a lot of overlapping classes, when the schedules are finally ready in august/beginning of september. However you can change your course enrollments until the end of september which gives a lot of flexibility. However some of the courses I was hoping to get where full which resulted in that I where not able to get the combination of courses I was hoping for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The student advisory office could help with the applications for course enrollments and it was possible to do multiple enrollment applications to change courses. My experience was that the information needed to apply for course enrollments where all available online.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I would say that 2 out of 3 classes where exactly what I hoped for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: But in work to find the best combination of courses possible with your schedule. I spent a lot of time trying to make the puzzle add up and I believe it paid off.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In my experience, the level of courses was much like in Copenhagen. However, the participation of students in discussions was not as high as I am used to in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was quite similar. A mix of lectures and seminars.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Digital Global Development
The Anthropology of Energy in the Global South
Gender & Environment

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would highly recommend the 'Gender & Environment' course because it engages with critical ecofeminism (and so much more), which is something I have not had the chance to work with at the University of Copenhagen.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected costs beside transport which I were not planning on spending so much money on.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food in supermarkets was usually a bit less expensive than I had thought. Eating at restaurants was more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot! I recommend participating in all the fairs (sports fair, club fair etc.) in the beginning of the semester. Both academic and non-academic possibilities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Participating in some sort of sports activity. Because it is a nice way of meeting people from the uni and engaging with them in a more relaxed setting.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going on hikes, sleeping in bothys (the Scottish equivalent to shelter in Denmark), going on trips to the highlands, Isle of Skye, and exploring if there are any concerts or anything you would like to do. A lot of bars play live jazz music in the afternoon/evening as well. And all museums are free.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy I think.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: People were really sweet in my courses and I primarily socialized with them about our courses, readings and so. Also I think it is important to remind oneself that it is not because there is anything wrong with you if you have a hard time socializing with the local students. You are only there for a couple of months so I had the experience that a lot of locals did not engage too much with exchange students. But there are plenty of other exchange students to do a lot of fun stuff with.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any actually.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nature and theater is as well a big thing in Edinburgh.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Exiting courses and competent professors. 
2. Great if you want to explore beautiful nature while studying. 
3. Edinburgh is a University city and there are a lot of students, which is nice.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did however spent more time on my studies than I expected I would.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I went on exchange with 2 friends I already knew from Copenhagen. It was important for me that we had this experience together and could explore the country together.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from friends and family for a long time. Not being able to take a break in the same way.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
